body_markdown:
A storage unit can make a Chicago apartment move more manageable when lease dates, elevator reservations, furniture deliveries, or renovation schedules do not line up. Store furniture, boxes, and household items until your new apartment is ready, then retrieve items as you set up each room.


This can be especially useful when a River North or West Loop building limits service-elevator appointments, a Lakeview lease ends before a new unit is available, or a winter move requires more time between loading, parking, and delivery windows.


Public Storage has 110 storage facilities in the Chicago area, with unit sizes from lockers to 10×30. Select locations offer[drive-up storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/self-storage/drive-up-storage) ,[climate-controlled storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/climate-controlled-storage) ,[24/7](https://www.publicstorage.com/self-storage/24-hour-storage) Access, and[vehicle storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/vehicle-car-rv-storage) .


Chicago renters can compare storage near River North, Lincoln Park, Lakeview, West Loop, Wicker Park, Logan Square, Hyde Park, and the Loop.


## Chicago Apartment Move Storage Essentials:


- Use storage when your old lease ends before your new apartment is ready.
- Confirm service-elevator reservations, loading-zone rules, truck parking, and move-in hours before scheduling movers.
- Move bedding, everyday clothing, toiletries, work supplies, and basic kitchen items into the apartment first.
- Put away furniture, décor, books, seasonal clothing, and boxes you will not need during the first week.
- Label every box with the room, contents, and access priority.
- Keep boxes you expect to retrieve soon near the entrance of the storage unit.
- Leave a clear aisle through the unit for staged unpacking.

## What Storage Unit Size Do I Need for a Chicago Apartment Move?


The right storage unit size depends on your furniture, box count, and whether you need access to belongings during the move. Measure large furniture before reserving, especially sofas, mattresses, dining tables, shelving, and bed frames.


A 5×5 unit can work for boxes, décor, and seasonal items. A 5×10 unit can fit boxes, smaller furniture, and studio-apartment overflow. A 10×10 unit can fit furniture and boxes from many one-bedroom apartment moves, while a 10×20 unit can help with larger furniture loads or a staged multi-room move.


Unit sizes are approximate, and availability varies by location. Use the[Public Storage size guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) to compare common dimensions before reserving.


## How Can Storage Help During a Chicago Apartment Move?


Storage supports a staged Chicago apartment move when your old lease ends before your new apartment is available or when a building limits service-elevator appointments. It can also give you time to set up the bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, and work area before moving in every box.


**Put away items that are not needed during your first week:**


- Extra dining chairs
- Rugs, lamps, and décor
- Books and seasonal clothing
- Furniture awaiting final placement
- Boxes for rooms you are not setting up right away
- Extra kitchen items and serving pieces
- Shelving or storage furniture that may not fit the new layout


Keep everyday clothing, basic kitchen supplies, toiletries, essential work items, medication, and personal records with you. Do not store food, perishables, wet items, live plants, hazardous materials, or sensitive original documents.


## What Should You Ask Your Chicago Apartment Building Before Moving?


Chicago apartment buildings may have rules that affect when and how movers, delivery trucks, and furniture can access the property.


**Ask your building team these questions before confirming your move:**


- What move-in days and hours are available?
- Is a service-elevator reservation required?
- How far in advance must the elevator be booked?
- Where may moving trucks park?
- Does the loading zone have time limits?
- Do movers need proof of insurance or other documentation?
- Are large furniture deliveries limited to certain times?
- Are building projects, such as painting or flooring, restricted to certain hours?


The answers can help you decide whether storage is needed for a few days, several weeks, or longer.


## How Should You Organize Storage for a Staged Chicago Move?


Organize the unit by the order in which you expect to unpack. Keep boxes and furniture from the same apartment room together so you can retrieve them when that area is ready.


Storage Unit Area


What to Place There


Front


First-week boxes, work supplies, and items to retrieve soon


Left side


Living-room furniture and boxes


Right side


Bedroom furniture and boxes


Back


Seasonal items, décor, and boxes needed later


Center


Clear walkway for access


Label boxes on at least two sides. Use specific labels such as **Bedroom — First Night** , **Kitchen — After Cabinets Are Ready** , or **Office — Work Setup** instead of “Miscellaneous.”


Take photos of the completed layout and keep a simple inventory list on your phone. This can help you find a box without opening everything in the unit.


## Is Drive-Up Storage Available in Chicago?


[Drive-up storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/self-storage/drive-up-storage) lets you park near a ground-level unit door for loading and unloading. Public Storage has 101 Chicago-area locations with drive-up access.


Drive-up storage can help with sofas, mattresses, shelving, dining tables, boxes, and other bulky apartment items. It can be useful when you are making several trips between your old apartment, storage unit, and new building.


Compare drive-up storage in Chicago and check your selected location for current availability.


## Should I Choose Climate-Controlled Storage for a Chicago Move?


[Climate-controlled storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/climate-controlled-storage) provides a more consistent indoor environment for furniture, clothing, books, electronics, photographs, and décor. Public Storage has 56 Chicago-area locations with climate-controlled storage.


Chicago weather can include humid summers, rain, cold winters, snow, and seasonal temperature changes. Compare available climate-controlled units when you are storing household items between leases, during a renovation, or while waiting to move into a new apartment.


See current Chicago climate-controlled storage options before making your reservation.


## Can I Find 24/7 Access Storage in Chicago?


Yes. Public Storage has 99 Chicago-area locations with[24/7](https://www.publicstorage.com/self-storage/24-hour-storage) access. This can help when your service-elevator appointment, moving truck, work schedule, or furniture delivery does not fit standard hours.


For example, 24-hour access can help you retrieve a box of work supplies before an early workday or move boxes after a late elevator reservation. Confirm current access hours, entry requirements, and unit availability at your selected location before reserving.


## Create a Smoother Chicago Apartment Move.


Storage can help you move into a Chicago apartment in stages when lease dates, elevator appointments, delivery schedules, and room setup timelines do not align. Compare nearby unit sizes,[drive-up storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/self-storage/drive-up-storage) ,[climate-controlled storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/climate-controlled-storage) , and available access options before reserving.


Move in first. Unpack on your timeline.

**What Should I Put in Storage Before Moving Into a Chicago Apartment?**
Store nonessential furniture, décor, seasonal belongings, books, and boxes you will not need immediately. Keep bedding, toiletries, everyday clothing, work supplies, basic kitchen items, medication, and personal records with you.


**What Should I Ask My Chicago Apartment Building Before Moving Day?**
Ask about move-in hours, service-elevator reservations, loading-zone time limits, moving-truck parking, mover documentation, and large-delivery restrictions. These requirements can determine whether storage helps with your move timeline.
